name: Agriculture
blurb: Vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, and autonomous equipment at commercial scale, tracked through USDA ERS, FAO, satellite data providers, and the equipment and standards bodies.

points.desc: Deere's precision agriculture line (See and Spray, autonomous tractors) is the reference commercial deployment.
points.name: Precision ag is shipping product

points.desc: Census BTOS covers agriculture-adjacent sectors in its fortnightly AI-use series.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The Economic Research Service publishes the data series on precision-agriculture adoption across US farms - variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, autonomous equipment. The federal measurement layer.
points.name: USDA ERS measures US adoption

points.desc: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization's digital agriculture program, with the 60 Decibels-supported Digital Agriculture Index, benchmarks platform adoption and real-world yield and income impact.
points.name: FAO benchmarks digital agriculture globally

points.desc: The AgriFoodTech investment research tracks venture capital into agricultural AI, robotics, computer vision, and farm-management software - the sector's funding barometer.
points.name: AgFunder indexes the investment flow

points.desc: Planet Labs' high-resolution imagery, Descartes Labs' geospatial ML, and EarthDaily's field-level crop indicators supply the AI-ready observation data behind yield prediction and crop-stress detection.
points.name: The satellite layer feeds the models

points.desc: The Association of Equipment Manufacturers covers autonomous machinery, AI hardware standards, and robotics adoption across crop and livestock production.
points.name: AEM tracks the machinery standards

points.desc: The nonprofit consortium sets the open data standards that let AI models ingest feeds from tractors, drones, soil sensors, and satellites - the plumbing under everything else.
points.name: AgGateway makes the data interoperable

points.desc: The International Society of Precision Agriculture is the scientific organization connecting academic research on remote sensing and spatial analytics to commercial practice.
points.name: ISPA bridges the science and the field

points.desc: The 100 Million Farmers initiative tracks AI adoption through the lens of climate-smart and regenerative agriculture metrics globally.
points.name: WEF tracks climate-smart adoption

points.desc: Bayer's Climate FieldView and Corteva's Granular are the large digital-farming platforms turning soil, weather, and yield data into planting and input prescriptions with machine learning.
points.name: The agribusiness platforms run the prescriptions

points.desc: CNH Industrial's Raven division builds driverless tractor technology, AI path-planning, and precision application - the equipment layer beyond Deere.
points.name: CNH and Raven automate the other fleets

points.desc: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder kills weeds with computer vision and lasers instead of herbicide; Monarch builds electric driverless tractors - narrow AI shipping as farm equipment.
points.name: The pure-plays attack single problems

summary: Precision agriculture - vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, autonomous equipment - is deployed at commercial scale. Who tracks it: federal adoption data, a UN benchmarking framework, a venture index, and standards bodies, layered over the equipment giants and AI pure-plays actually shipping it.

analysis.body:
The Census Bureau's measurement of AI adoption in agriculture remains suppressed, limiting direct federal visibility into how widely farms are deploying these tools. However, complementary data sources reveal active commercial deployment and investment momentum. Per AgFunder, global agrifoodtech funding reached $16.2 billion in 2025, nearly flat versus the prior year but with investors directing capital more selectively toward companies with tangible science and clear paths to revenue. This disciplined funding environment reflects a sector moving past early hype toward proven use cases.

Commercial AI deployment in agriculture concentrates in three domains. Per Climate FieldView, farmers using seed scripts saw an average increase of +5 bu/ac compared to users who wrote their own scripts, demonstrating measurable ROI from machine learning-driven input prescriptions. Per Carbon Robotics, autonomous solutions like the LaserWeeder use large plant models trained on the world's largest agricultural dataset to reduce costs and eliminate weeds while increasing yields. Per Raven Industries, a Brand of CNH, automated and autonomous farm technologies are designed to improve productivity, sustainability, and profitability across precision agriculture solutions. The satellite and geospatial layer underpins these prescriptions: Planet Labs provides daily high-resolution Earth data and analytics that power crop monitoring and stress detection models at scale.

The infrastructure enabling AI deployment is fragmented across standards and data interoperability layers. AgGateway works to promote and enable the industry's transition to digital agriculture through data standards that let AI models ingest feeds from tractors, drones, soil sensors, and satellites. The Association of Equipment Manufacturers brings agricultural equipment OEMs together to understand data and develop strategies around autonomous machinery, AI hardware standards, and robotics adoption. This standards work remains foundational because farm AI depends on reliable data flows across equipment and sensor networks that historically operated in silos.

Investment geography shows uneven adoption readiness. Per AgFunder, agrifoodtech funding in Asia-Pacific raised $4.2 billion as of the end of October 2024, a 38% increase on the $3.1 billion raised over the same period in 2023, while African agrifoodtech funding showed mild growth with $145 million in the first half of 2024, a 1.6% year-over-year increase but just 1.6% of global investment. Developing markets grew substantially between 2023 and 2024 at 63% versus a 4% decline in global agrifoodtech, suggesting that capital is flowing to regions with infrastructure and scale advantages.

The scientific and equipment manufacturing communities have aligned around precision agriculture as the organizing framework. The International Society of Precision Agriculture bridges academic research on remote sensing and spatial analytics to commercial practice, while the USDA Economic Research Service measures adoption of variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, and autonomous equipment across US farms as the federal measurement layer. John Deere's precision ag product line, including See and Spray and autonomous tractors, remains the reference commercial deployment. A farm deciding whether to deploy should weigh proven incremental gains like the +5 bu/ac observed with Climate FieldView scripts against the capital cost of hardware, the dependency on reliable data standards and satellite or sensor feeds, and regional readiness of equipment service networks and software interoperability.

https://www.ispag.org/.brief: The International Society of Precision Agriculture is a scientific organization that develops technologies to help feed the world and improve quality of life. It offers a definition of precision agriculture in more than fifteen languages and gives members access to directories, networking, and discounted conference registration. Members receive a monthly “ISPA newsletter” that shares news, job listings, and event information, and the society is preparing for the 17th ICPA and 11th ConBAP in summer 2026. Country Representatives promote ISPA worldwide; applicants must email info@ispag.org with a bio, CV, and be current members, and members can post job announcements on the site and in newsletters.

https://www.planet.com/.brief: Planet Labs offers a platform called Planet Insights that brings together daily satellite imagery, derived data products, and cloud-based tools in one place. The company claims its imagery is the highest-frequency commercial Earth observation data, enabling daily monitoring, high-resolution tasking, and deeper derived insights. It says the platform lets users view the planet in time, space, and frequency, helping them make decisions quickly and confidently. Planet reports that organizations across many sectors use the platform to address operational challenges with a global, dynamic perspective.

https://www.ers.usda.gov/.brief: The page is the homepage of the Economic Research Service, which focuses on food, farming, natural resources, and rural America. It offers State Fact Sheets that cover population, income, poverty, food security, education, employment, farm characteristics, farm financial indicators, top commodities, and agricultural exports, with data for all states, metro/nonmetro breakouts, and Puerto Rico, plus county links where available. The Food Price Outlook section provides food price data and forecasts for changes in the Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index for food. Users can also access Vegetables and Pulses Data, a collection of statistics on fresh and processed vegetables and dry pulses in the United States and some global data, and can subscribe to email notifications for updates.

https://agfunder.com/research/.brief: AgFunder reports that global agrifoodtech funding reached $16.2 billion in 2025, down 3% year-over-year, with investors becoming more selective and favoring companies demonstrating "tangible science, real unit economics, and clear paths to revenue." While overall funding remained relatively flat, regional patterns diverged significantly: developing markets agrifoodtech grew 63% between 2023 and 2024, Asia-Pacific startups raised $4.2 billion as of October 2024 (a 38% increase), and African agrifoodtech showed mild recovery with $145 million raised in the first half of 2024 after a 62% decline in 2023. These trends suggest a sector undergoing consolidation, with capital concentrating in regions and companies meeting stricter investment criteria.

https://www.fao.org/digital-agriculture/.brief: FAO reports that the first stage of the Global AgriInno Challenge 2026 selected 13 youth-led innovation solutions from 137 valid applications out of 191 total, giving them a chance to pitch in China. The page explains that e-Agriculture is a global community of practice created from Action Line C7 ICT Applications of the World Summit on the Information Society, with FAO as its facilitator, and that its mission is to promote dialogue on the use of ICTs for sustainable agriculture and rural development. FAO also notes that three youth-led initiatives, AgriKonnekt from Kenya, Berikanpreneur from Indonesia, and a third unnamed, won the final pitch event in Hangzhou on 10 September 2026. Additionally, the page records that the 30th Session of the Committee on Agriculture (COAG 30) held in Rome from 20 to 24 July 2026 concluded after a week of high-level discussions on the future of agriculture and food systems.
